title: Rome
lead: Rome, a city in Italy, became master of the Mediterranean in the last two centuries BC. It first appears in Jewish writings as a distant ally (1 Maccabees 8), took Jerusalem under Pompey in 63 BC, ruled Judea through Herod and its governors in Jesus's day (Luke 2:1; Luke 3:1), destroyed the temple in AD 70, is where Paul's last journey ends (Acts 28), and in most readings is the "Babylon" of Revelation (Revelation 17–18).
